title: Spelling Team Champion
goal: I can spell words with ea and oo, and pick the right team.

card.desc: Bristol proves she can spell with the ea team (long e) and the oo team (the moon sound and the book sound), all mixed up. She picks the team by the middle sound, fixes words like red, bock and skool, and writes words from dictation. Page 2 of the packet is a spelling test Tia reads aloud over the break. The break work is light, so the Holiday Gazette comes first.

win: Spelling Team Champion! Have a happy break! ❄️

teacher.objective: Bristol proves she can spell and read words with the ea team (long e, plus the few that say short e) and the oo team (the moon sound and the book sound), mixed together. She picks the right team by the middle sound, tells a team from a single short vowel, fixes misspelled words (red → read, bock → book, skool → school), and writes words from dictation. Week 7 Day 3 (Prove it). Last lesson before the winter break.
materials: The Class lesson open on your laptop (course page, code 9110)
Tuesday's 10 oo cards, plus 8 new cards: beach, read, dream, clean, school, food, book, look
Printed packet (2 pages) to send home. Show Tia the spelling test on page 2.

Class slide 6. ea, oo, e or o.

Class slides 11–12. Whiteboard first, then typed.

Class slide 16. Show the break task list (first week, second week). The Holiday Gazette comes first.

watch: Mixing the teams (meen or mean for moon, toom for team). Ask: "Long e, or the moon sound?"
One letter where a team is needed (bock, mon, bech, clen). Ask: "Is it a short sound, like bed or hot? If not, use a team."
red for read and bock for book: her own mistakes. Praise every time she gets them right.
skool or scool for school. It is a word to remember: s-c-h-o-o-l.
Reading head, bread or feather with long e. Remind her: try long e first; if it does not make sense, try short e.

packet_key.answer: The food is on the table.
Any sentence that uses two of the spelling words, spelled right, with a capital letter and a period.

teacher.notes: Last lesson before the winter break. The Holiday Gazette (Dec 20 – Jan 3) comes first; this task list is light and split into the first and second week of the break. Page 2 of this packet is a spelling test Tia reads aloud (the word list is at the bottom of page 2, to fold back). Ask Tia to send a photo of page 2 before Lesson 19 (Zoom), or have Bristol hold it up to the camera then. If she scores under 85 on Show What You Know, she retakes it (new set) in the first week of the break, after 5 minutes with the word cards. The next lesson is Lesson 19 (Zoom), where the girls present the Holiday Gazette.

tasks: Thursday night: do the After-Class Lesson. Finish with Show What You Know.
First week of the break: do the Lesson 18 Practice.
First week of the break: do page 2 of the Lesson 17 Packet (the page you saved).
First week of the break: do the reading lesson Reading Foundations: Vowel Team Sentences. Read sentences with vowel teams smoothly. Aim for 90. If it is locked, type 1111.
Second week of the break: do the Lesson 18 Packet. On page 2, Mom reads the spelling test to you. Show it to Jonathan at Lesson 19.
Second week of the break: do the reading lesson Reading Foundations: Vowel Team Mix & Read. Read words with every vowel team you know. Aim for 90. If it is locked, type 1111.
Both weeks of the break: read your book for 15 minutes a day, 4 days a week. Your Holiday Gazette comes first! You show it at Lesson 19 on Zoom.
